paper_title: Getting the most on supernova axions
notes: Paper presents supernova bounds on ALP-nucleon coupling from SN 1987A. Main constraints: (1) Modified luminosity criterion excludes g_aN ≳ 6×10^-10 for m_a ≲ 1 MeV (combining free-streaming and trapping regimes); (2) Kamiokande-II non-observation of ALP-induced oxygen excitation excludes g_aN ≳ 3×10^-7 for m_a ≲ 20 eV. The paper uses KSVZ benchmark model with g_an = 0 (neutron coupling set to zero), so constraints are primarily on g_ap (proton coupling). However, the abstract and main text refer to 'ALP-nucleon coupling g_aN' generically. The coupling type is labeled as AxionNeutron per the pre-analysis hint, but the paper's benchmark (KSVZ with Can=0) actually constrains the proton coupling g_ap. The data points encode: (1) lower bound from cooling ~6×10^-10 for m_a ≲ 1 MeV (horizontal line); (2) upper bound from cooling ~2.5×10^-6 for m_a ≲ 10 MeV; (3) upper bound from cooling ~3.5×10^-7 for m_a ~ 100 MeV; (4) lower bound from KII ~3×10^-7 for m_a ≲ 20 eV. Mass ranges are approximate; bounds vary with mass. Confidence is 0.85 rather than 0.9 because the paper's primary coupling is g_ap (proton) under KSVZ, not a generic nucleon or neutron coupling, creating some ambiguity in the coupling_type assignment. | selector: text (sole candidate)
